differences.what: The flat top now has real two-row openings, corner pinnacles, a checker band and five colonnettes dividing six upper windows.
The south bow has three basement lights, three principal transom openings and four second-storey sashes; the north loggia has paired Ionic columns and a pierced lower panel.

T-2565's loggia, compared at this view's scale (T-2577): Glessner's front and the tree in front of 1808 hide the loggia; only the top of the balcony's south pedestal shows, so this view cannot judge its carving or columns.

T-2566's granite, compared at this view's scale (T-2577): the tree's crown covers the front's checker band and courses and Glessner's roof hides the bow; the north return's courses are T-2564's item above.
Hidden rear elevations and concealed roof surfaces cannot be accepted from this front photograph.
The earlier low stone boundary replaces the generic iron fence with urns. Its exact post/rail sections remain reconstructed.

T-2564: the north return is laid in large dressed courses (about 0.46 m) with staggered joints, 5.5 m long as the course counts in the 1887-89 and 1948 views give it, where it was a smooth 2.8 m slab.
The original is monochrome; granite colour is not shown. Sepia/scan casts are not material colour.
T-2578: this print does not resolve the corner behind the rear pinnacle (trees and grain); the stone parapet's stop there is ruled from the views that see it.

T-2577: the cornice box under the lattice is laid in the front's dressed stone, so the crown reads as one stone mass from the wall head to the lattice, as the photographs show it; the brown band is gone in this render.

T-2714: the checker band's units are pitched 0.28 m along their rows (0.336 m before), with 0.07 m of ground between neighbours, as the 1888 Keith plate lays them; the rows are unchanged. Not judged here: Keith's front is foreshortened beyond reading the band's units.

T-2748 (the reviewer's reason for this verdict): this file is the owner's reproduction of the c. 1888 SW photograph, cropped (the crown above the third-storey lights is out of frame, so the pinnacles, the return's coping and the cowl are not shown here) and about a third of the blog copy's size, now on that view's re-fitted camera. In register, the third-storey lights, the bow and the north arris lie on the print's; the stoop does not, and reads here as it does in the c. 1888 view: its landing's pierced balustrade and the low round arch under its flight stand left of the render's (the arch at about x 296-305 against 310-321 at this file's scale) and the arch far lower than built. The record differs on that alone. Open for the build (carried on T-2751).
